subject.title: Device identity generation should not depend on browser Secure Context — breaks HTTP reverse-proxy deployments

question: Should browser Control UI device identity be allowed after the UI is delivered over non-localhost plain HTTP, and if yes should that be default behavior or an explicit insecure opt-in?
rationale: The remaining change decides whether persistent operator browser identity can be trusted when the page itself may have been tampered with in transit, which is a maintainer security/product boundary rather than a mechanical SHA-256 helper fix.

options.title: Keep Secure-Context Requirement
options.body: Continue requiring HTTPS or localhost for browser device identity and rely on trusted-proxy, Tailscale, break-glass, docs, and warning mitigations for self-hosted deployments.

options.title: Add Explicit Insecure Opt-In
options.body: Allow pure-JS browser identity only behind a clearly named insecure Control UI flag with audit warnings, docs, and tests for default-blocked and opt-in behavior.

options.title: Allow Plain HTTP By Default
options.body: Remove the secure-context gate and WebCrypto digest dependency by default, accepting a broader remote-plaintext trust model for Control UI operators.

recommendation.title: Keep Secure-Context Requirement
recommendation.body: Continue requiring HTTPS or localhost for browser device identity and rely on trusted-proxy, Tailscale, break-glass, docs, and warning mitigations for self-hosted deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: The core decision traces to secure Control UI auth and device-bound connect challenge history that steipete introduced and recently carried forward.
